definitions.explanation: The act or manner of walking. A literary or formal alternative to the everyday word for walking.
The figurative path or trajectory of development over time. Used for the history or progress of an organization, person, or movement.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{歩|あゆ}み⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{止|と}めた→止める：00678_tomeru⟧。
⟦{疲|つか}れて→疲れる：00901_tsukareru⟧{歩|あゆ}み⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{遅|おそ}く→遅い：00533_osoi⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。

examples.english: I headed home with heavy steps through the snow.

notes:
USAGE:
The noun form of the verb ⟦{歩|あゆ}む→歩む：13196_ayumu⟧. Sense 1 (walking) is literary and used in written or formal contexts; everyday speech prefers ⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧こと. Sense 2 (progress/history) is the more common usage in modern Japanese, especially in book titles, exhibition descriptions, and organizational histories.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {歩|あゆ}み⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{進|すす}める→進める：01949_susumeru⟧: to advance, to make progress
- {歩|あゆ}み⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{止|と}める→止める：00678_tomeru⟧: to stop walking / to halt progress
- {歩|あゆ}み⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{振|ふ}り{返|かえ}る→振り返る：04231_furikaeru⟧: to look back on one's journey
- ⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{歩|あゆ}み: the course of history
